title: Fleet Janitor: lease-based autoscaling negotiation protocol for throughput-preserving maintenance
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: During rolling maintenance and upgrades, Dedicated fleets currently experience transient throughput cliffs when multiple hosts are drained simultaneously or when KV cache warm-up cannot keep up. Existing approaches rely on coarse reservation lanes and centralized orchestration which can be brittle at scale.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight distributed "Fleet Janitor" service and a lease-based autoscaling negotiation protocol. The Janitor coordinates (1) incremental host handoffs, (2) short-lived throughput leases that let nodes 'bid' to accept more traffic while preserving SLOs, and (3) preheat/kv-cache warming hints to downstream nodes. The negotiation protocol is optimistic, eventual-consistent, and designed to minimize central lock contention.

Core pieces: 
- Lease allocator: issues time-limited throughput leases (token buckets) per host slice. Leases are transferable and can be split for partial drains.
- Bid protocol: hosts under drain advertise residual capacity and KV cache heat metrics; candidate hosts respond with acceptance bids including predicted latency delta.
- Janitor controller: evaluates bids using a scoring function (latency delta, cache-heat, locality, commit-priority) and issues transfer actions.
- Graceful drain adapter: drain actions apply ramp functions (linear or sigmoid) to traffic weights and emit preheat hints to recipients.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Centralized vs distributed leasing: chosen hybrid model to avoid single-point bottleneck while keeping global safety checks.
- Lease length: longer leases reduce churn but increase risk of stale allocations; default 90s with jitter. Tunable per-customer.
- Scoring complexity: start with simple weighted sum and telemetry-derived weights; move to ML ranking only if necessary.

Observability & SLOs: 
- New metrics: lease_acquire_latency, lease_revoke_errors, bid_accept_rate, preheat_success_ratio, kv_warmup_time.
- Dashboards: "Fleet Janitor — Current Leases" and "Maintenance Wave Health".
- Alerts: sustained drop >5% throughput or p99 latency regressions during maintenance window.

Rollout plan: 
1) Canary in non-prod fleets: Janitor controller read-only mode for 2 weeks to gather telemetry.
2) Canary with simulated transfers (no actual shift) in staging.
3) Gradual enable in low-load dedicated fleets (10% traffic) with 1-day observation.
4) Full rollout with opt-out per-customer.

Safety knobs: max_transfer_rate per host, hard SLA fallback to existing reservation lanes, manual override in Console, automatic rollback on consecutive alerts.

Artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Fleet+Janitor+Design, initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-infra/pull/2897, prototype dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/Janitor123, perf runbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/ops/janitor-runbook.md
comments: 2025-02-13 - Maya Chen: Initial draft and design spike completed. Collected microbenchmarks for KV warmup windows. Posting doc to Confluence for PM/Design review.

2025-02-18 - Diego Alvarez: Implemented prototype lease allocator + in-memory bid store. Observed race when two Janitor replicas grant overlapping leases; adding vector-clock style lease ids to avoid double-grant.
2025-02-22 - PM review (Anika Rao): Suggested feature flag per-customer and per-fleet controls; approved scoring function start as telemetry-driven weights.

2025-02-24 - SRE (Lucas Brandt): Request adding circuit-breaker to revoke transfers if KV preheat failure rate > 15% over 5m. Noted need for tracing hooks to link drain actions with token-level cost spikes.

2025-02-27 - Diego Alvarez: Added simulated-canary harness and synthetic traffic test. Results: p95 latency preserved within 3% for 1k concurrent qps, KV preheat recovered at ~45s median. Need to improve preheat hints to lower warmup to <30s.
2025-03-01 - Maya Chen: Security signoff not required for initial rollout; will revisit if adding cross-tenant telemetry aggregation. Scheduling canary for 2025-03-05.
